plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; if I bid lower, I risk losing a profitable opportunity. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) when I win, there's no incentive to shade my bid. Therefore, my optimal strategy is to bid exactly my value of $31, regardless of my beliefs about Betty and Charles's strategies.

In a second-price auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do, since the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if you win against a bid between your true value and your bid; underbidding risks losing the item when you would have profited. Therefore, with a value of $46, the optimal and safest strategy is to bid exactly $46.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others bid or believe, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $35, ensuring maximum expected profit.
